PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY LESSON · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Playground — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the playground — how each piece works and the two big rules that make it fun for everyone.

What is this?

A playground is a place built for playing: a slide, swings, a climbing frame, usually on soft ground, usually full of other kids doing exactly the same thing.

What does it mean?

Turn-taking is the idea: the best slide in town is best because everyone gets a turn — the playground is sharing, made out of metal and sunshine.

What does the child need to know?

You need grippy shoes, turn-taking patience, and the two big rules loaded: one at a time on the slide, and never grab a moving swing.

Why this matters

Wiggles have to go somewhere — the playground is where they go to be used up, loudly, with other children, in the fresh air.

What it teaches

Climbing strength, turn-taking, swing pumping (lean and stretch — the rhythm finds itself), and the brave first slide of every new season, when the slide looks taller than last year.

Words to learn

playgroundslideswingladderclimbturnwaitpumproundaboutmerry-go-round

Say this to your child

“"The playground! Up the ladder — step, step — check the bottom is clear... WHEEE, down the slide! Off, away, back of the line. Now the swings — lean back, pump, pump — higher! The playground is where the wiggles live!"”

Step by step

  1. Up the ladder — step, step, step, hands hold the rails.
  2. Top of the slide: sit, check that nobody is at the bottom, then... WHEEE! Feet first, always.
  3. Off, away, and to the back of the line — one at a time is the rule, and the line moves fast when everyone follows it.
  4. The swings: sit, lean back, pump the legs — stretch, fold, stretch, fold — higher, higher!
  5. The circuit: one turn on everything, then a favorite — and when the swing must stop, let it stop. Never grab a moving swing; waiting is a playground superpower.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, all three classics ride together — the slide, the swing frame and the climbing ladder — the trio every playground in the world is built around.

Ask your child

"What do we check before we slide?" (nobody at the bottom) "How do we go higher on the swing?" (lean back and pump the legs) "What are the two big rules?" (one at a time on the slide — never grab a moving swing)

What your child can say or do

Your child might run the circuit with referee-level rule enforcement, discover swing-pumping on a random Tuesday and demand witnesses, or name the slide like a roller coaster with a grand opening every spring.

Out in the real world

British playgrounds often add a roundabout (the US says merry-go-round), and the see-saw answers to teeter-totter across the border — every town names the same joy differently. Swings are the starter: pumping by yourself is a real independence day.

Try it together

Playground circuit: one trip on each thing, then choose a favorite and do it three more times. Teach the two big rules kindly — one at a time on the slide, and wait for the swing to stop before you grab it.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we do at the top of the slide?" (sit, check, then feet first) "What do we do when we want the swing?" (wait for it to stop — never grab it)

This lesson pairs with the Playground flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Places in the Community.
